subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 2 medium / 98 hard. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: Pronase is distinct from enzymes like trypsin or chymotrypsin in protein chemistry because it:

options.A: Is a single enzyme with very narrow specificity for one bond
options.B: Is a mixture of non-specific proteolytic enzymes that causes complete hydrolysis of a protein down to free amino acids
options.C: Only cleaves carbohydrate-protein bonds in glycoproteins
options.D: Cannot hydrolyse peptide bonds at all

questions.explanation: Pronase is a mixture of non-specific proteolytic enzymes that, unlike the more selective trypsin/chymotrypsin/pepsin/elastase, causes complete hydrolysis of a protein all the way down to its free amino acids — useful for determining total amino acid composition rather than sequence.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Determination of Primary Structure
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Which advice following total hip replacement is INCORRECT?

options.A: Keep a pillow between your legs while sleeping
options.C: When turning, pivot on the operated leg

questions.explanation: Pivoting on the operated leg combines rotation and adduction with the foot fixed and risks dislocation. Patients should take small steps to turn.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A characteristic finding in reaction of degeneration on galvanic testing is:

options.A: Absent response to direct current in all cases
options.B: Cathodal closing contraction much greater than anodal closing contraction with brisk response
options.C: Polarity reversal — anodal closing contraction becomes equal to or greater than cathodal closing contraction

questions.explanation: In normal muscle CCC > ACC with brisk twitches. In RD, contraction is sluggish (vermicular), faradic response is lost and ACC ≥ CCC (polarity reversal).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which finding would NOT be expected with a C6 root lesion?

options.A: Paraesthesia of the middle and ring fingers
options.B: Sensory loss over the thumb and lateral forearm
options.D: Weakness of biceps and wrist extensors

questions.explanation: C6 root: thumb/index sensory loss, biceps and wrist extension weakness; the middle finger is C7 and ring/little C8.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Stretching of collagenous tissue is most effective when it is performed:

options.C: With cold tissue and quick force
options.D: After warming the tissue, with a low-load, long-duration stretch

questions.explanation: Heat increases collagen extensibility; low-load prolonged stretch produces plastic (permanent) elongation with less risk of tearing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: ‘Pointing index’ (inability to flex the index finger when making a fist) indicates a lesion of the:

options.B: Median nerve (anterior interosseous branch) or median nerve at the wrist/forearm

questions.explanation: Median nerve paralyses FDS and the lateral half of FDP, so the index (and middle) finger remain extended when making a fist.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Under conditions of fatigue or cognitive overload, the brain tends to:

options.A: Shift towards more careful, deliberate Type 2 thinking
options.B: Revert to Type 1 (fast, intuitive) processing to conserve cognitive energy, increasing the risk of bias-driven error
options.D: Show no measurable change in decision-making style

questions.explanation: The brain regions required for effortful Type 2 processing are most affected by fatigue and cognitive overload; under these conditions the brain reverts to faster, less effortful Type 1 processing to conserve energy — which is exactly when cognitive biases are more likely to lead to error.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: A Theraktin tunnel (bank of fluorescent tubes) is used for:

options.A: General (whole-body or large-area) UV irradiation, e.g. in psoriasis

questions.explanation: The Theraktin tunnel is a semi-circular cradle of long-wave UV fluorescent tubes giving general irradiation; it is used for conditions such as psoriasis often with coal tar (Leeds regimen).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A disease is suitable for population screening if:

options.B: It is an important health problem with a recognisable latent stage and an effective treatment

questions.explanation: Wilson and Jungner criteria.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The classical needle-EMG finding in a primary myopathy is:

options.A: Short-duration, low-amplitude polyphasic motor unit potentials with early full recruitment
options.B: Fasciculations as the only abnormal finding
options.C: Giant, long-duration motor unit potentials with reduced recruitment
options.D: Complete electrical silence on voluntary effort

questions.explanation: In myopathy muscle fibres drop out from each motor unit, so potentials become small and brief; many units are needed for little force, giving early recruitment.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The proportion of ultrasound energy reflected at an interface between two media depends mainly on:

options.A: The frequency of the mains supply
options.C: The temperature of the transducer only
options.D: The difference in acoustic impedance of the two media

questions.explanation: The greater the difference in acoustic impedance, the greater the reflection — almost total at an air–tissue interface and high at a soft tissue–bone interface (periosteal burning risk).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: How does the metabolic response to trauma/sepsis differ from simple starvation regarding ketone formation?

options.A: Both produce identical, unimpaired ketone formation
options.B: In trauma/sepsis, ketone formation is impaired, and glucose-generating protein breakdown cannot be entirely prevented even by giving glucose
options.C: Trauma always increases ketone formation far beyond that seen in starvation
options.D: Ketone formation is irrelevant to both conditions

questions.explanation: Unlike simple starvation (where glucose administration can readily reverse protein catabolism), trauma and sepsis patients have impaired ketone formation, and gluconeogenesis (protein breakdown to make glucose) cannot be entirely prevented by giving exogenous glucose — a key nutritional distinction between the two states.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Nutrition and Fluid Therapy — Metabolic Response to Trauma and Sepsis
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: True phimosis, as distinguished from a normal non-retractile foreskin in a young boy, is characterised by:

options.A: Simple inability to retract the foreskin at age 2, which is entirely normal
options.B: Whitish scarring of the foreskin caused by balanitis xerotica obliterans (BXO), rarely seen before age 5
options.C: Ballooning of the foreskin during urination with no scarring
options.D: A condition that always requires surgery in infancy

questions.explanation: 'Phimosis' is often wrongly applied to a normal non-retractile foreskin, which is common and physiological in young boys. True phimosis is pathological whitish scarring caused by balanitis xerotica obliterans (BXO), and is rare before 5 years of age.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — The Foreskin and Circumcision
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The Employees' State Insurance (ESI) scheme provides:

options.C: Medical care and cash benefits to workers in case of sickness, maternity or employment injury

questions.explanation: Covers employees of establishments with 10 or more workers earning up to the prescribed wage limit.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A 'retractile' testis is distinguished from a true undescended testis by the fact that:

options.A: A retractile testis can be manipulated without tension into the base of the scrotum, though it is pulled back up by the cremaster muscle
options.B: A retractile testis is always impalpable
options.C: A retractile testis requires orchidopexy immediately
options.D: There is no meaningful difference between the two

questions.explanation: A retractile testis can be brought down to the base of the scrotum without tension, but is then pulled back up by an overactive cremaster reflex — over time it usually resides permanently in the scrotum, though follow-up is still advised as it can rarely re-ascend and require orchidopexy.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — Undescended Testes
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Tendons heal slowly compared with muscle mainly because:

options.B: Of relatively poor vascularity and low metabolic activity
options.D: They contain too many blood vessels

questions.explanation: Hypovascular zones (e.g. supraspinatus critical zone, Achilles) have limited healing capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: What is the minimum daily urine output generally required to adequately excrete the end products of protein metabolism?
questions.explanation: A minimum urine output of approximately 400 mL/day is required to excrete the nitrogenous end products of protein metabolism, even though average daily urine output in a healthy adult is around 1500 mL/day.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Which ion is delivered from the negative electrode (cathode) to soften adherent scar tissue?
questions.explanation: Chloride is negatively charged and repelled from the cathode; used for scar and adhesions. Acetate (negative) is used for calcific deposits. Zinc and lidocaine are positive ions delivered from the anode.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In a child presenting with acute scrotal pain, testicular torsion must be relieved within approximately what time window from symptom onset for a good chance of testicular salvage?
questions.explanation: Testicular torsion must be relieved within 6-8 hours of symptom onset for a good chance of salvaging the testis — this is why any acute scrotum where torsion cannot be confidently excluded requires urgent surgical exploration.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — The Acute Scrotum
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Posterior internal impingement of the shoulder, commonly seen in overhead athletes, occurs when the rotator cuff impinges against the posterosuperior edge of the glenoid, with the arm positioned in:

options.C: Complete elbow flexion with the shoulder neutral
options.D: Full flexion with the forearm pronated

questions.explanation: Posterior internal impingement occurs when the arm is abducted, extended, and laterally rotated — a position common in the late cocking phase of throwing — causing the rotator cuff to impinge against the posterosuperior glenoid rim, sometimes producing a 'kissing' labral lesion.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Posterior Internal Impingement Test
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In fat necrosis due to acute pancreatitis, free fatty acids released from ruptured adipocytes combine with calcium to form:
questions.explanation: In fat necrosis, liberated pancreatic lipases cause hydrolysis of adipocytes, releasing free fatty acids which complex with calcium to form calcium soaps — a process called saponification, giving the necrotic foci their firm, chalky-white gross appearance.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Cell Injury, Cellular Adaptations and Cellular Ageing — Fat Necrosis
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Vojta therapy for infants is based on:

options.A: Reflex locomotion elicited through pressure on specific zones

questions.explanation: Reflex creeping and reflex rolling stimulated from trigger zones to activate normal motor patterns.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In a patient with COPD and chronic CO2 retention, oxygen therapy is titrated to a saturation of about:
questions.explanation: High FiO2 can suppress hypoxic drive and worsen hypercapnia; controlled low-flow oxygen (Venturi mask) is used.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Syringomyelia classically produces:

options.A: Dissociated sensory loss (pain and temperature lost, light touch preserved) in a cape distribution with hand weakness
options.C: Loss of all sensation below the lesion

questions.explanation: Expansion of the central canal damages decussating spinothalamic fibres, producing ‘suspended’ sensory loss and painless burns.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A rotator cuff tear is LEAST likely in:

options.A: A patient younger than 40 years with no trauma
options.B: A patient with weakness of external rotation
options.C: A patient over 60 with night pain
options.D: A patient with an altered scapulohumeral rhythm

questions.explanation: Rotator cuff tears are typically degenerative in older patients; in young patients they follow significant trauma.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Active insufficiency occurs when:

options.B: A multi-joint muscle is shortened over all its joints and cannot generate effective force
options.C: A muscle is stretched over two joints

questions.explanation: Example: making a tight fist with the wrist fully flexed is weaker because finger flexors are shortened.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Haemozoin (acid haematin, malarial pigment) is distinguished from haemosiderin by which key laboratory feature?

options.A: Haemozoin stains positive with Perl's Prussian blue reaction, while haemosiderin does not
options.B: Haemozoin does NOT stain with Perl's Prussian blue reaction, unlike haemosiderin which does
options.C: Both stain identically with every histochemical stain
options.D: Haemozoin is only found in bone marrow, never other tissue

questions.explanation: Unlike haemosiderin, haemozoin (malarial pigment) does NOT stain with Perl's Prussian blue reaction — likely because it forms a complex with protein that prevents the reaction — despite both being haem-iron-derived pigments.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.sourceChapter: Cell Injury, Cellular Adaptations and Cellular Ageing — Acid Haematin
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Diastasis recti abdominis is:

options.C: Separation of the two rectus abdominis muscle bellies along the linea alba
options.D: A fracture of the pubic symphysis

questions.explanation: Common in late pregnancy; avoid double leg raises and sit-ups; transversus abdominis activation is taught.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Apparent shortening of the leg with normal true leg length is typically due to:

options.D: Pelvic obliquity (e.g. adduction contracture of the hip)

questions.explanation: True length equal but apparent length reduced implies pelvic tilt or fixed adduction deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Kleine-Levin syndrome, a rare recurrent hypersomnia, classically also includes which additional feature?
questions.explanation: Kleine-Levin syndrome is classically characterised by recurrent hypersomnia (always present) along with hyperphagia (usually present, a voracious appetite), and sometimes hypersexuality — predominantly affecting males with onset in the second decade of life.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: Why is a scaphoid fracture through the waist of the bone at particular risk of avascular necrosis?

options.A: The scaphoid has no nutrient artery at all
options.B: Both nutrient arteries typically enter through the distal part (tubercle/body), so a waist fracture can cut off blood supply to the proximal fragment
options.C: The scaphoid is the only carpal bone with no cartilage covering
options.D: Scaphoid fractures always damage the ulnar nerve directly

questions.explanation: The scaphoid's blood supply normally enters via nutrient arteries at the tubercle (palmar surface) and the dorsal surface of the body — both relatively distal. A waist fracture can therefore deprive the proximal fragment of its blood supply, since retrograde flow to that fragment is often insufficient, leading to avascular necrosis and a high risk of nonunion.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Carpal Bones, Clinical Anatomy
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Diadynamic currents (Bernard) are derived from:

options.A: Rectified 50 Hz mains sine waves (half-wave MF at 50 Hz and full-wave DF at 100 Hz)
options.B: Alternating current of 4000 Hz and 4100 Hz

questions.explanation: Diadynamic currents use half- or full-wave rectified sinusoids — MF (monophasé fixé, 50 Hz), DF (diphasé fixé, 100 Hz), CP, LP and RS modulations. They are unidirectional with a galvanic component.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In a setting with a high local prevalence of C. difficile, why is alcohol gel decontamination between patient contacts considered inadequate?

options.A: Alcohol gel is more effective than hand-washing against C. difficile spores
options.B: Alcohol gel does not kill C. difficile spores, so hands must be washed with soap and water instead
options.C: C. difficile cannot be transmitted via hands under any circumstances
options.D: Alcohol gel damages skin more than soap and water

questions.explanation: Alcohol gel decontamination is usually adequate for routine hand hygiene, but it does not kill C. difficile spores. In situations of high C. difficile prevalence (e.g. a local outbreak), hands must be washed with soap and water instead, since spores survive alcohol-based decontamination.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Infection Prevention and Control — Health Care-Associated Infection
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The final descent of the testis into the scrotum during fetal development is mediated primarily by:

options.C: Growth hormone from the fetal pituitary

questions.explanation: While gonadal induction (forming a testis in the first place) is driven by genes on the Y chromosome and initial abdominal migration is guided by the gubernaculum, the final descent of the testis into the scrotum is mediated by testosterone produced by the fetal testis itself.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Paediatric Surgery — Genital Development
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Clot retraction, which produces a more effective and compact haemostatic plug, is driven by contraction of platelet pseudopodia containing which contractile protein?
questions.explanation: Clot retraction (the fibrin clot contracting to about 40% of its original volume within 5-30 minutes) is produced by contraction of platelet pseudopodia, which contain the contractile actomyosin-like protein historically called thrombosthenin.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A clinician decides to keep a patient in hospital 'just in case', despite evidence-based guidelines and a completed systematic assessment supporting discharge, because they recently encountered a similar rare case. This is an example of which cognitive bias?

options.C: Commission bias only, unrelated to availability

questions.explanation: Availability bias occurs when a recent or memorable case distorts a clinician's estimate of probability, making a rare condition seem more likely simply because it is 'at the forefront of the mind' — exactly as described, overriding a systematic (Type 2) assessment with an irrational intuitive override.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Common Cognitive Biases
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: During the acute stage of myositis ossificans, which treatment is contraindicated?

options.D: Active-assisted range of movement within pain limits

questions.explanation: Massage and passive stretching can worsen bleeding and promote heterotopic ossification.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Proprioception and vibration sense are carried in the:
questions.explanation: Dorsal columns: fine touch, vibration, proprioception (ipsilateral until the medulla). Spinothalamic: pain and temperature (contralateral).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Dislocation of the lunate bone (from a fall on the acutely dorsiflexed hand) typically displaces it in which direction, and can mimic the features of which condition?

options.A: Displaces posteriorly; mimics De Quervain's tenosynovitis
options.B: Displaces anteriorly; can produce carpal tunnel syndrome-like features
options.C: Displaces laterally; mimics ulnar nerve palsy at the elbow
options.D: Does not displace, only rotates in place with no clinical effect

questions.explanation: Dislocation of the lunate is produced by a fall on the acutely dorsiflexed hand with the elbow flexed; it displaces the lunate anteriorly, where it can compress the median nerve within the carpal tunnel, producing carpal tunnel syndrome-like features.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Carpal Bones, Clinical Anatomy
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: To stimulate healing in a clean indolent ulcer or pressure sore with UV, the dose commonly applied is:

options.B: A high erythemal dose, e.g. E3–E4, to the margins and base

questions.explanation: High erythema doses cause exfoliation of necrotic tissue and stimulate granulation. Infected wounds require UVC/short UV with higher dosage.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The D-dimer test has high sensitivity but low specificity for pulmonary embolism. What does this mean in practice?

options.A: A positive D-dimer confirms pulmonary embolism definitively
options.B: A negative D-dimer helps rule out pulmonary embolism, but a positive result does not confirm it — it only means the disease has not been excluded
options.C: The D-dimer test is useless in clinical practice
options.D: High sensitivity and low specificity mean the test is always accurate regardless of result

questions.explanation: A highly sensitive test detects most true disease (few false negatives), so a negative result is reassuring and helps exclude the disease. But low specificity means many people without the disease will still test positive (false positives) — so a raised D-dimer does not confirm pulmonary embolism, it simply means it cannot yet be excluded, prompting further imaging.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Interpreting Test Results
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: When treating a patient with dementia the therapist should:

options.D: Use simple short instructions, a consistent routine and demonstration

questions.explanation: Cognitive impairment limits learning of new skills; use demonstration, repetition and familiar tasks.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Charcot's triad of multiple sclerosis consists of:

options.C: Nystagmus, intention tremor and scanning speech

questions.explanation: Reflects brainstem/cerebellar involvement: nystagmus, intention tremor, scanning (staccato) speech.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) in mechanical ventilation:

options.A: Keeps alveoli open at the end of expiration, improving oxygenation

questions.explanation: PEEP prevents alveolar collapse but may reduce cardiac output and cause barotrauma at high levels.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The existence of 'spare receptors' (receptor reserve) explains which observed phenomenon?

options.A: Some full agonists can produce a maximal response while occupying less than 1% of available receptors
options.B: All antagonists eventually become agonists at high enough doses
options.C: Receptor numbers never change regardless of chronic drug exposure
options.D: Enzymes and receptors are functionally identical structures

questions.explanation: When a tissue has a large receptor reserve, a full agonist can produce its maximal biological response by occupying only a small fraction of the total available receptors — occupying more receptors beyond that doesn't increase the effect further, since the response has already plateaued.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: To improve the reliability of goniometric measurement between sessions you should:

options.A: Use the same patient position, landmarks, instrument and preferably the same tester
options.B: Change landmarks each time to avoid bias

questions.explanation: Standardising technique reduces error; intratester reliability is better than inter-tester.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Alternating isometric contractions of agonists and antagonists without movement to promote stability is called:
questions.explanation: Rhythmic stabilisation improves co-contraction and stability, e.g. in trunk or weight-bearing control.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Why is the metaphysis of a growing long bone especially important clinically when it lies partly within a joint capsule?

options.A: It has no blood supply, so infection cannot spread there at all
options.B: Being an actively growing, richly vascularised part of the bone, infection there can spread into the joint if the metaphysis is intracapsular (and vice versa)
options.C: It is always extracapsular in every long bone, so it never affects joints
options.D: It only matters in the lower limb, not the upper limb

questions.explanation: The metaphysis is the actively growing part of the bone adjacent to the epiphyseal line, with a rich blood supply — making it a common site for infection in young people. Where the metaphysis is partly or wholly intracapsular (as at the upper end of the humerus), joint infection can spread to the metaphysis, and metaphyseal disease can spread into the joint.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Capsular Attachments and Epiphyseal Lines
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Muscle energy technique (MET) uses:

options.A: The patient's own isometric contraction against a counterforce, followed by relaxation and stretch

questions.explanation: MET (Mitchell): patient contracts a muscle isometrically against a controlled counterforce (post-isometric relaxation), then the therapist takes up the new barrier.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A common complication after severe traumatic brain injury that can limit range of motion at the hip and elbow is:
questions.explanation: Spasticity and immobility predispose to new bone formation in muscle near large joints.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: When you move your head, objects nearer than your fixation point appear to move in the OPPOSITE direction to your head movement, while objects farther than the fixation point move in the SAME direction. This is the depth cue of:
questions.explanation: This is the movement (motion parallax) cue for depth: objects closer than the fixation point appear to move opposite to head movement, while objects farther than the fixation point move in the same direction — and the amount of apparent movement is smaller for distant objects than for near ones.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Sensory Processes and Perception — Monocular Cues for Depth Perception
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: Rood's approach to neurological rehabilitation primarily uses:

options.A: Sensory stimulation (brushing, icing, tapping) to influence muscle tone

questions.explanation: Rood used cutaneous stimulation (quick brushing, icing, stroking), proprioceptive stimuli and ontogenetic sequence of postural patterns.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A hamartoma is best defined as:

options.A: A malignant tumour of embryonal blastema seen mainly in infants
options.B: A benign tumour composed of mature but disorganised cells/tissues that are normally indigenous to that organ
options.C: An ectopic island of otherwise completely normal tissue in the wrong location
options.D: A tumour combining epithelial and mesenchymal malignant elements

questions.explanation: A hamartoma is a benign lesion made up of mature, differentiated tissue elements that are normal to the organ in question, just disorganised/jumbled — e.g. a pulmonary hamartoma contains mature cartilage, smooth muscle, and epithelium, all normal bronchial components arranged abnormally. This is distinct from a choristoma (ectopic normal tissue in the wrong site) and from blastomas (embryonal tumours of children).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: An ABG shows pH 7.30, PaCO2 60 mmHg and normal bicarbonate. This is:
questions.explanation: Low pH with high PaCO2 and normal HCO3⁻ indicates uncompensated respiratory acidosis (e.g. acute ventilatory failure).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Acetic acid iontophoresis for calcific tendinitis relies on delivering which ion?
questions.explanation: Acetate is an anion; like charges repel, so it is driven into tissue from the cathode, where it may help dissolve calcium deposits.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Before cervical manipulation, which test screens for vertebrobasilar insufficiency?
questions.explanation: Sustained extension/rotation tests look for dizziness, nystagmus, diplopia, drop attacks (the 5 Ds and 3 Ns).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Permanent hardness of water is due to the presence of:

options.D: Sulphates and chlorides of calcium and magnesium

questions.explanation: Temporary hardness (bicarbonates) is removed by boiling.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Early strength gains observed in the first 2-3 weeks of a resistance training program are primarily attributed to:

options.B: Neural adaptation, since significant hypertrophy/vascularization changes typically require at least 6-12 weeks
options.C: An increase in the total number of muscle fibers (hyperplasia)

questions.explanation: Strength gains in the first 2-3 weeks of resistance training are mainly the result of neural adaptation (improved motor unit recruitment and coordination), not muscle tissue change. Significant hypertrophy or increased vascularization typically requires at least 6-12 weeks of consistent training.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The (modified) Wells score is a clinical prediction rule used to estimate pre-test probability for which condition?
questions.explanation: The Wells score is a clinical prediction rule used to estimate the pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism (and, in another version, deep vein thrombosis), helping guide which further tests (e.g. D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiogram) are appropriate.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Clinical Prediction Rules
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome from PICA/vertebral occlusion presents with:

options.A: Contralateral hemiplegia with ipsilateral tongue deviation
options.B: Total paralysis with vertical eye movement preserved
options.D: Ipsilateral facial pain/temperature loss and contralateral body pain/temperature loss with ataxia and dysphagia

questions.explanation: Spinothalamic (contralateral body) and spinal trigeminal (ipsilateral face) involvement, with cerebellar ataxia, hoarseness, dysphagia and Horner's syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which tissue absorbs ultrasound energy MOST per unit thickness?

options.D: Bone and other tissues rich in collagen and protein

questions.explanation: Absorption is highest in tissues with high protein/collagen content such as bone, tendon and ligament; lowest in fluid and fat.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The Na+-K+ pump is described as 'electrogenic at rest' because it operates with a coupling ratio of 3 Na+ out for every 2 K+ in. What would happen to its contribution to the membrane potential if the coupling ratio were instead 1:1?

options.A: It would generate an even larger membrane potential
options.B: It would not directly generate any membrane potential itself, though it would still maintain the concentration gradients the potential depends on
options.C: The cell would immediately depolarise completely and stay depolarised
options.D: The pump would stop functioning altogether

questions.explanation: At a 3:2 coupling ratio, the Na+-K+ pump moves net positive charge out of the cell with each cycle, directly contributing a small electrogenic component to the membrane potential. If the ratio were 1:1 (equal charge moved each way), the pump itself would not generate any net potential directly — though it would still be essential for maintaining the ionic concentration gradients that the resting membrane potential fundamentally depends on.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: The Membrane Potentials — Genesis of Resting Membrane Potential
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a second-class lever in the body?

options.C: Elevating the arm with the deltoid

questions.explanation: Calf muscle effort is at the heel (calcaneus) with the resistance (body weight through the tibia) lying between the axis (toes) and the effort.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Hyperventilation produces which acid–base disorder?
questions.explanation: Blowing off CO2 reduces carbonic acid and raises pH; symptoms include perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: 'Subinvolution' and 'superinvolution' of the uterus refer respectively to:

options.A: Delayed/incomplete involution, and a smaller-than-normal uterus sometimes seen with continued lactation
options.B: Two names for exactly the same clinical finding
options.C: Involution occurring only in the cervix versus only in the vagina
options.D: Terms with no real clinical distinction from normal involution

questions.explanation: Subinvolution refers to involution proceeding more slowly or incompletely than expected. Superinvolution, by contrast, describes a uterus that becomes smaller than normal, sometimes seen in lactating women — a change that reverses if lactation is withheld.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.sourceChapter: Normal Puerperium — Clinical Assessment of Involution
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Passive insufficiency of a two-joint muscle is demonstrated when:

options.B: A muscle cannot develop tension because it is already shortened
options.D: The muscle is stretched over both joints so that full range at the second joint cannot be achieved (e.g. hamstring tightness limiting hip flexion with knee extended)

questions.explanation: Active insufficiency: the muscle is shortened over both joints and cannot produce force; passive insufficiency: the antagonist is stretched across two joints and limits motion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: When naming a peptide, the amino acid suffixes (e.g. '-ine' in glycine) are changed to '-yl' for every residue EXCEPT which one?

options.C: Any residue in the middle of the chain

questions.explanation: In peptide nomenclature, every amino acid's suffix is changed to '-yl' except the C-terminal residue, which keeps its normal name. For example, a tripeptide of glutamate-cysteine-glycine (glycine being C-terminal) is named glutamyl-cysteinyl-glycine.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Peptide Bond
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Compared with parallel muscle fibres, pennate muscles of the same volume have:

options.C: A larger physiological cross-sectional area, producing greater force but less excursion

questions.explanation: Pennation packs more fibres per unit volume; examples: gastrocnemius, deltoid, rectus femoris.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Persistence of red-coloured lochia well beyond the normal expected duration most likely signifies:

options.A: Normal healing with no clinical concern
options.B: Subinvolution of the uterus or retained bits of the conceptus
options.C: A completely normal variant seen in all women
options.D: Onset of the first postpartum menstrual period

questions.explanation: Persistence of the red colour of lochia beyond the normal limit is a clinically important sign suggesting subinvolution of the uterus or retained products of conception, and should prompt further evaluation.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: In arthrometer testing, the 'quadriceps active position' refers to the knee angle at which:

options.A: The tibia shows no forward movement when the quadriceps contracts, typically around 70° of flexion
options.B: The knee is fully extended at 0°
options.C: The patient is asked to relax completely with no muscle contraction
options.D: The hamstrings are maximally contracted instead of the quadriceps

questions.explanation: The quadriceps neutral (active) angle is the knee flexion angle — typically around 70° — at which an isolated quadriceps contraction produces no anterior tibial translation in a normal knee; this position is used as a reference when testing the injured knee for abnormal anterior displacement (suggestive of PCL injury).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Joint play movements are:

options.A: Small involuntary accessory movements within the joint that cannot be performed actively

questions.explanation: Roll, glide and spin occur passively and are essential for full range of motion (Mennell).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In patients with hypertension, which type of exercise should be limited?
questions.explanation: Isometric effort and breath-holding cause marked rises in blood pressure; dynamic aerobic exercise lowers resting BP.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: To increase knee flexion by joint mobilisation, the tibia (concave) should be glided:
questions.explanation: The tibial plateau is concave, so it glides in the same direction as the shaft moves in flexion (posterior). The patella is also glided inferiorly for flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Creep in connective tissue refers to:

options.C: Progressive deformation under a constant load over time
options.D: A decrease in force at a constant length

questions.explanation: Low-load prolonged stretching exploits creep; stress relaxation is the decrease in stress when held at constant length.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Which type of impulse is able to stimulate denervated muscle selectively while avoiding stimulation of surrounding normal innervated muscle and sensory nerves?

options.B: A short-duration, rapidly rising faradic pulse
options.C: A slowly rising, long-duration (e.g. triangular or trapezoidal) pulse

questions.explanation: Normal nerve accommodates to slowly rising currents and does not fire, whereas denervated muscle fibres have lost the ability to accommodate and respond to slow-rising, long-duration pulses.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Bronchiolitis in infants is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: RSV causes small airway inflammation with wheeze; treatment is supportive.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In acute respiratory distress syndrome, a key supportive position that improves oxygenation is:
questions.explanation: Prone positioning recruits dorsal lung regions and improves V/Q matching; used for at least 12–16 hours/day in severe ARDS.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The most reliable early clinical sign of compartment syndrome is:

options.C: Pain out of proportion to the injury, worsened by passive stretch of the muscles in the compartment

questions.explanation: Pain on passive stretch is the earliest sign. Pulselessness, pallor and paralysis are late; diagnosis is clinical, with pressure measurement when uncertain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: To increase lateral rotation of the glenohumeral joint, the humeral head should be mobilised with:
questions.explanation: Convex–concave rule: humeral head (convex) on glenoid (concave); the head glides in the direction opposite to the bone motion. Lateral rotation needs anterior glide; medial rotation needs posterior glide.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Within the femoral sheath, which compartment contains the femoral canal (occupied by a lymph node), and which structure occupies the intermediate compartment?

options.A: The medial compartment is the femoral canal; the femoral vein occupies the intermediate compartment
options.B: The lateral compartment is the femoral canal; the femoral artery occupies the intermediate compartment
options.C: The femoral nerve occupies the femoral canal
options.D: There is only one compartment in the femoral sheath

questions.explanation: The femoral sheath has three compartments: the lateral compartment contains the femoral artery, the intermediate compartment contains the femoral vein, and the medial compartment is the femoral canal, occupied by a lymph node (and providing space for femoral vein distension, and the path for femoral hernias).
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Lower Limb
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) promotes:
questions.explanation: JSY is a safe-motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The Nernst equation is used in physiology to calculate:

options.A: The equilibrium potential for a specific ion, based on its concentration gradient across the membrane
options.B: The total resting metabolic rate of a cell
options.C: The rate of action potential propagation along an axon
options.D: The molecular weight of an ion

questions.explanation: The Nernst equation calculates the equilibrium potential for a given ion — the membrane potential at which the electrical force on that ion exactly balances its concentration gradient, so there is no net movement of that ion across the membrane.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.sourceChapter: The Membrane Potentials — The Equilibrium Potential
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A relative risk of 1.0 indicates:

options.B: No association between exposure and outcome

questions.explanation: RR >1 increased risk; RR <1 protective.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A choristoma differs from a true neoplasm in that it is actually:

options.A: An ectopic island of otherwise normal tissue (heterotopia), not a genuine tumour
options.B: A tumour with two distinct malignant cell lines mixed together
options.C: Exactly the same thing as a hamartoma
options.D: Always fatal within the first year of life

questions.explanation: A choristoma is the name given to ectopic islands of completely normal tissue found in an abnormal location — it is heterotopia, not a true tumour, even though the name sounds like one.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Platelets are formed by pinching off bits of cytoplasm from which giant, multinucleated bone marrow cell?
questions.explanation: Platelets are formed within the cytoplasm of the granular megakaryocyte by pinching off bits of cytoplasm, released into circulation when the cell dies — a single megakaryocyte can produce 2,000-4,000 platelets by this process.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The ‘unhappy triad’ of the knee (O'Donoghue) consists of injury to the ACL, MCL and:
questions.explanation: Classically ACL + MCL + medial meniscus (many modern series show the lateral meniscus is more often torn with acute ACL injury).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The 'plane of least pelvic dimensions' (narrow pelvic plane), a landmark used for pudendal nerve block, corresponds anatomically to approximately the level of:

options.D: The pubic symphysis alone, excluding any posterior landmark

questions.explanation: The plane of least pelvic dimensions extends from the lower border of the symphysis pubis to the tip of the ischial spines, and posteriorly to the 5th sacral vertebra. It is the narrowest plane in the pelvis, roughly corresponds to the origin of levator ani, is where internal rotation of the fetal head occurs, and is the landmark used for pudendal nerve block.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.sourceChapter: Fetal Skull and Maternal Pelvis — Outlet
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: In deep transverse friction massage (Cyriax) the therapist:

options.A: Slides along the skin using oil
options.D: Moves the tissue back and forth perpendicular to the direction of the fibres without sliding on the skin

questions.explanation: No lubricant is used so that the skin moves with the fingers and the deep tissue is mobilised; used in tendinitis and ligament sprains.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In ‘pusher syndrome’ following stroke, the patient:

options.A: Pushes away from the hemiparetic side
options.C: Actively pushes toward the hemiparetic side and resists correction to the midline

questions.explanation: Contraversive pushing is associated with a disturbed perception of the body's vertical (posterior thalamus). Treatment uses visual feedback to realign to the vertical.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In a patellar tendon-bearing (PTB) transtibial prosthesis the main weight-bearing areas are the:

options.A: Patellar tendon and pressure-tolerant areas such as the medial tibial flare
options.B: Head of the fibula and tibial crest
options.D: Distal end of the residual limb

questions.explanation: The PTB socket is relieved over the tibial crest, fibular head and distal end (pressure-intolerant) and loads the patellar tendon and medial tibial flare.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Hip subluxation in spastic cerebral palsy is most commonly due to spasm of the:
questions.explanation: Adductor and iliopsoas tightness with weak abductors lead to hip migration; surveillance with pelvic X-ray is routine.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In NYHA class III heart failure the patient:

options.B: Has marked limitation: comfortable at rest but less-than-ordinary activity causes symptoms
options.C: Has no symptoms with ordinary activity

questions.explanation: Class I no limitation; II slight limitation; III marked limitation; IV symptoms at rest.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which patellar glide is needed to improve knee FLEXION?
questions.explanation: As the knee flexes the patella slides distally; a restricted inferior glide limits flexion, whereas a restricted superior glide limits extension.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Compared with normal gait, a patient using crutches (non-weight bearing) has:
questions.explanation: Crutch walking requires 2–3 times the oxygen consumption of normal gait for amputees and non-weight-bearing patients.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: If different-sized electrodes are used in the coplanar method, the heating effect is:

options.B: Concentrated under the smaller electrode, where field density is higher

questions.explanation: A smaller electrode gives a higher field density, hence more heating beneath it. Equal-sized electrodes give an even distribution.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The thermal effect of pulsed shortwave diathermy becomes evident when the mean power output exceeds about:
questions.explanation: Pulsed SWD with a mean power under about 5 W is considered athermal; above this level heating occurs. Pulsed energy is chosen for acute conditions.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Glucocorticoid receptors are unique among the major receptor families in that they:

options.A: Are located on the cell surface and open ion channels directly
options.B: Are intracellular soluble proteins that, once liganded, dimerize and bind DNA to regulate gene transcription
options.D: Have no known endogenous ligand (are 'orphan receptors')

questions.explanation: Glucocorticoid receptors sit in the cytoplasm bound to HSP-90 and other inhibitory proteins. When the lipid-soluble steroid penetrates the cell and binds the receptor, HSP-90 is released, the receptor dimerizes, and the complex moves to the nucleus to bind glucocorticoid-responsive elements (GREs) on DNA, altering gene transcription — a fundamentally different, much slower mechanism than membrane receptors.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: When an apparent outbreak of infection is investigated and 'typing' shows the causal organisms do NOT share identical phenotypic/genotypic characteristics, the event is instead termed a:
questions.explanation: Confirmation of a genuine infectious disease outbreak usually requires typing evidence that the causal organisms share identical phenotypic and/or genotypic characteristics. If this is not the case, the apparent cluster is termed a pseudo-outbreak rather than a true outbreak.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Epidemiology of Infection — Outbreaks of Infection
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Posterior interosseous nerve syndrome causes:

options.B: Wrist drop with sensory loss in the first web space
options.C: Finger drop without wrist drop and without sensory loss

questions.explanation: The PIN is the motor continuation of the radial nerve below the supinator; ECRL is spared so the wrist extends with radial deviation.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Using the KT-1000 arthrometer, a difference of more than 3 mm in anterior displacement between the injured and uninjured knee is generally considered:

options.A: A normal finding requiring no further action
options.B: Diagnostic for injury to the anterior or posterior cruciate ligament
options.C: Evidence of a meniscal tear specifically, never a ligament injury

questions.explanation: A side-to-side difference of more than 3 mm in anterior displacement on KT-1000 arthrometer testing is generally considered diagnostic for injury to the anterior cruciate ligament or posterior cruciate ligament.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition
